topic: Physical and Chemical Changes in Matter
key_concepts: Physical change alters form, size, shape, or state without forming a new substance
Cutting, grinding, breaking, pounding, powdering, and stretching cause physical changes
Phase changes include melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, sublimation, and depos
Chemical change forms one or more new and different substances
Chemical changes are usually irreversible and involve rearrangement of atoms
Clues of chemical change include color, odor, and taste changes
Effervescence, precipitation, and heat loss or gain can indicate chemical change
Rusting and browning of foods are chemical changes in the presence of oxygen
Burning and cooking can cause chemical changes through application of heat
Spoiling, souring, and decay are chemical changes
No new product is formed in physical change; new products form in chemical change
